notes:
I've organised my notes on Revelation 11 verse by verse, with the URL after each point. A few things to know first:

- **The main split:** In this chapter the biggest disagreement isn't between denominations. It's between two ways of reading Revelation. Futurist and dispensational teachers (Guzik, MacArthur, Walvoord, Precept Austin) read the temple and the witnesses as real and still future. Idealist and historical readers (Ellicott, Storms, the Gospel Coalition, Gill, Matthew Henry) read them as pictures of the church. Both camps include people from several traditions.
- **What I couldn't find:** I found nothing on Revelation 11 from Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org), Anglican sources, bibleodyssey.org or netbible.org notes. I also found nothing on how prosperity, word of faith or hyper-grace teachers use this chapter. Those sections are left out.
- **Weak spots:** The Enduring Word page cut off partway through verse 11. Verses 14 and 16–18 have only thin coverage.

---

**v. 1 – Measuring the temple**
- Guzik (Pentecostal-leaning) says the temple is most likely a literal Jewish temple yet to be rebuilt in Jerusalem (not merely a symbol of the church). He argues the passage has too much detail to be a general picture of the church, and he takes measuring to mean God owns and controls the place. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Ellicott: The measuring, like the sealing of Revelation 7, is a sign of preservation during impending dangers. The measured part is the inner temple (Greek *naos*), and its point is the preservation of the true, invisible Church, the Church within the Church. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-11.html
- Gill (Baptist, 1700s) applies the measuring to his own time. He identifies the baptized and congregational churches as the measured temple, set against national state churches. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/11-1.htm
- Adam Clarke (Methodist) thinks the verse must refer to the Jerusalem temple, which he takes as another presumptive evidence that it was yet standing when John wrote. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-1.html
- Barclay says the measuring is closely parallel to the sealing and is for the purposes of protection. He connects the image to the hopes of the Zealots (Jewish rebels) before Jerusalem fell in AD 70. Same URL.

**v. 2 – The outer court and the 42 months**
- Guzik suggests the outer court might be where the Dome of the Rock stands, though he admits the research is by no means settled. He places the trampling in the last half of a future seven-year period. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Ellicott takes the outer court as worldliness inside the church. He says the 42 months need not be literal: they stand for a limited period under God's control, the church's time of pilgrimage. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/11.htm
- Storms (charismatic, amillennial) says 42 months, 1,260 days and 3½ years all mean the whole of this present church era, the time between Christ's first and second comings. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13
- Wesley takes the 42 months as ordinary months, a short, harsh treading-down near the end. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/11.htm

**v. 3 – The two witnesses** (the most disputed verse in the chapter)
- **Moses and Elijah:** MacArthur (Baptist) won't be dogmatic, but sees a number of reasons that suggest that they may be Moses and Elijah. He says they are real preachers, not symbols. https://shop.gty.org/library/bibleqnas-library/QA0087/who-are-the-two-witnesses-in-revelation-11
- **Two future men in the spirit of Moses and Elijah:** Bible.org says they are not literally those prophets but two men whom God will raise up in the spirit and power of their Old Testament counterparts. https://bible.org/seriespage/temple-two-witnesses-and-seventh-trumpet-rev-111-19
- **No firm answer:** GotQuestions lists three main theories (Moses and Elijah, Enoch and Elijah, two unknown believers) and concludes The Bible does not say. https://www.gotquestions.org/two-witnesses.html
- **The church:** The Gospel Coalition argues they represent the church's identity as the voice of God on the earth. There are two because of the two-witness rule in Deuteronomy 19:15. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/witnesses-revelation-symbolism/
- Storms puts it this way: you are the two witnesses! https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13
- Wesley (Methodist) sees two real prophets: two select, eminent instruments, preaching that Jesus is the Son of God and calling everyone to repent. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/11.htm
- Gill (historicist) says no two individual persons can be meant, since these witnesses were to prophesy 1260 days, that is, so many years, but a succession of ministers and churches. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-3.html
- Matthew Henry, on the same page, says they are God's eminent faithful ministers who keep preaching in the worst of times. Same URL.
- Sackcloth: Ellicott calls it the mourning dress the prophets wore, like the clothing of Elijah and John the Baptist. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/11.htm
- **History of the debate:** A Bible Hub article says Tertullian and Hippolytus held to Enoch and Elijah, and that The Reformers (Luther, Calvin) saw the passage as symbolic of the gospel-preaching church under persecution. That is the article's own summary; I didn't read Luther or Calvin directly. https://biblehub.com/q/Who_are_Revelation_11_3_s_two_witnesses.htm

**v. 4 – Olive trees and lampstands**
- The image comes from Zechariah 4. Guzik reads it as the witnesses' continual empowering from the Holy Spirit, first applied to Joshua and Zerubbabel. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Precept Austin expects that, Like Joshua and Zerubbabel, the two witnesses will lead a spiritual revival of Israel culminating in the building of a temple. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-11-commentary
- Storms points out that in Revelation 1:20 lampstands are churches, so the two lampstands are the church giving its witness. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13
- Coffman (Restoration Movement) notes that only two of the seven churches in chapters 2–3 were faithful. On that basis he reads the lampstands as "the faithful portion of the church". https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-4.html

**v. 5 – Fire from their mouths**
- Guzik says God protects them specially, as he did Elijah in 2 Kings 1. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Precept Austin argues that if figurative language is afoot, it is minimal. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-11-commentary
- Storms takes the fire as the power of the spoken word, like the sword from Christ's mouth and Jeremiah 5:14. The "harm" they are protected from is spiritual: persecutors can kill the body but not the soul. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13

**v. 6 – Drought, blood and plagues**
- These echo Elijah (James 5:17–18) and Moses (Exodus 7–12). Guzik adds that the Greek words for the witnesses are masculine, so in his view they are definitely two men. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Wesley asks: how is it possible to understand this otherwise than of two individual persons? https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-11.html
- Storms links shutting the sky to the power of believers' prayers, citing James 5. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13

**v. 7 – The beast kills them**
- Guzik's main lesson: they die only after The two witnesses complete their full testimony. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Matthew Henry: They are immortal, they are invulnerable, till their work be done. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-3.html
- Wesley calls them among the last martyrs, though not the last of all. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/11.htm

**v. 8 – "Sodom and Egypt"**
- Guzik takes the city as Jerusalem, described with three labels: Sodom (immorality), Egypt (oppression) and "the great city" (a name Revelation uses for Babylon). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Precept Austin: Jerusalem, in her godless state, is likened to both the wicked city and the wicked nation. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-11-commentary
- Storms says the singular "body" in verses 8–9 (Greek) supports reading the witnesses as the church. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/revelation-11:1-13---part-ii

**v. 9 – The whole world sees them**
- Guzik thinks this may hint at worldwide live broadcasting, and stresses how shameful it was to be left unburied. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Storms (quoting Beale) says the whole world seeing them fits best if they stand for the global church. He notes that Hal Lindsey's answer was television. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13

**v. 10 – The world celebrates**
- Precept Austin says the celebration shows how hard their plagues had hit. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-11-commentary
- Guzik says their call to repentance tormented people who loved their lie. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Matthew Henry: the witnesses had teased, terrified, and tormented the consciences of their enemies. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-3.html

**v. 11 – Raised after three and a half days**
- GotQuestions: they will be resurrected and, in full view of their enemies, ascend to heaven. https://www.gotquestions.org/two-witnesses.html
- Bible.org (Walvoord) treats their death, resurrection and ascension as literal. https://bible.org/seriespage/11-two-witnesses-and-seventh-trumpet
- Storms on the church reading: in the end we will be vindicated. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/the-church-prophesying-and-persecuted--revelation-111-13

**v. 12 – "Come up here"**
- Precept Austin places the witnesses within the "first resurrection," along with Christ's resurrection and the rapture of church saints. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-11-commentary

**v. 13 – Earthquake, 7,000 killed, the rest give glory**
- Walvoord takes the 7,000 as seven thousand individuals who die in the catastrophe. https://bible.org/seriespage/11-two-witnesses-and-seventh-trumpet
- Wesley reads "gave glory" as real repentance: The character of true conversion. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/11.htm
- Precept Austin sees this as part of turning ungodliness ... away from a portion of Jacob, meaning Israel. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-11-commentary

**v. 14 – The third woe**
- One commentary simply notes The "third woe" is also the seventh trumpet. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/tbs/meaning/rev-11-v15-19.cfm

**v. 15 – The seventh trumpet**
- Guzik says the past tense "has become" shows absolute certainty that Christ will reign, even before it is fully accomplished. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- Storms agrees the tense looks ahead to a certain future. He says the verse describes Christ's return and eternity, not this present age. https://www.samstorms.org/enjoying-god-blog/post/when-the-kingdom-of-the-world-has-become-the-kingdom-of-christ
- Ellicott stresses the singular "kingdom": the contest is for the kingdom of the world as a whole, not for separate nations. https://biblehub.com/revelation/11-15.htm
- **Older readings tied to history:**
  - Trapp (Puritan) says these kingdoms have renounced Popery ... and received the Reformation. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/kjv/revelation/11-15.html
  - Haydock (Catholic) applies it to the Roman empire becoming Christian by his raising Constantine the great. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-15.html

**vv. 16–18 – The elders worship**
- Guzik notes that "Almighty" (Greek *pantokrator*), used in v. 17, appears nine of its ten New Testament times in Revelation, and means the one with his hand on everything. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-11/
- DeYoung (Reformed): on that day the nations will no longer rage, the saints will be rewarded, the wicked destroyed, and God himself will be with us. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/blogs/kevin-deyoung/sermon-on-kingdom-of-god-revelation_06/

**v. 19 – The ark in the heavenly temple**
- Ellicott: the innermost room is opened, as if the temple veil were torn again, revealing the secret abode of the safe-guarded children of God. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/11-19.htm
- Gill sees Christ as the fulfilment of the ark. Hendriksen (quoted by Coffman) calls it a symbol of perfect fellowship with God based on the atonement through the blood of the Lord Jesus Christ. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-19.html
- Spurgeon (Baptist) preached on this verse, starting from the point that THE ARK OF HIS COVENANT IS ALWAYS NEAR TO GOD. https://www.spurgeon.org/resource-library/sermons/the-ark-of-his-covenant/
- Wesley says John saw it for a testimony, that what God had promised, should be fulfilled to the uttermost. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/11.htm
- Kelly (Brethren, dispensational) reads it as the resumption therefore of the old links with His ancient people Israel. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/11-19.html
- **Catholic reading:** Catholic Answers links the ark here to Mary in chapter 12: The Mary/ark imagery appears again in Revelation 11:19 and 12:1-17. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/ark-of-the-new-covenant. It also ties this to Mary's Assumption into heaven. https://shop.catholic.com/blog/marys-rapture/
- Meyer's commentary notes that most apply the ark to Christ, while Cornelius a Lapide (Catholic) want to refer it especially to the Virgin Mary, yet without denying the reference to the humanity of Christ. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/11-19.htm
- A Protestant reply (John Brown) says outright This is not the virgin Mary as the Catholic church teaches it to be! https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/brown_john/Rev/Chap_12.cfm

**Orthodox view (vv. 3–12):** The OCA's answer says Elijah and Enoch seems to be the commonly held opinion of many Church Fathers, with Moses and Elijah as another opinion. It adds that the witnesses may be examples of the faithful remnant who preach the Good News to people who reject it. https://www.oca.org/questions/scripture/two-witnesses-rev-111-14

**A pastoral caution (vv. 3–4):** Storms points out that many people in history have claimed to be the two witnesses. One example is two London tailors in the 1600s, whose followers, the Muggletonians, lasted for three hundred years. https://www.samstorms.org/all-articles/post/revelation-11:1-13---part-ii
